lines.trans: Life once again places us before a difficult choice.
We must fight on or simply submit to fate.
Friends, may I ask for a minute of your attention?
Congratulations, colleagues, now you are part of our family.
Our rules will give you the opportunity for rapid growth.
You will gain great experience in a good company.
We will start today with the main news.
Starting today, there is a new director in our restaurant.
And here she comes walking right this way.
Please welcome and respect—Viktoriya Sergeyevna!
Hello, I am the new director of the Claude Monet restaurant.
While we are thinking, completely new circumstances appear.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: У нас работает команда профессиональных поваров.
examples.trans: A team of professional chefs works here.

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот последняя банка, на, береги её.
examples.trans: Here is the last jar, take it and guard it.

examples.text: Вот молодцы, отлично испортили все блюда.
examples.trans: Well done, you ruined all the dishes splendidly.

examples.text: Вот это я сейчас серьёзно попал.
examples.trans: Now I have really gotten myself into trouble.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Они сюда слетелись, как коршуны.
examples.trans: They have flocked here like vultures.

examples.text: По каким ещё таким признакам?
examples.trans: By what kind of signs?

examples.text: Ох, какая тяжёлая у вас ситуация.
examples.trans: Oh, what a difficult situation you have.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф, а какая разница, кто будет зарабатывать?
examples.trans: Chef, what difference does it make who earns money?

examples.text: Смотри, сюда как раз Катя идёт.
examples.trans: Look, Katya is walking right this way.

examples.text: А почему сразу именно я должен доставать?
examples.trans: And why do I have to be the one to get it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: У нас работает команда профессиональных поваров.
examples.trans: A team of professional chefs works here.

examples.text: У нас обслуживание гостей на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: Our guest service is at the highest level.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У нас работает команда профессиональных поваров.
examples.trans: A team of professional chefs works here.

examples.text: А что, она тебе совсем не нравится?
examples.trans: What, do you not like her at all?

examples.text: Да нет, она очень хорошая девушка.
examples.trans: Well no, she is a very nice girl.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is coming', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Они сюда слетелись, как коршуны.
examples.trans: They have flocked here like vultures.

examples.text: Потому что нас всех отсюда выгонят.
examples.trans: Because they will kick all of us out of here.

examples.text: Смотри, сюда как раз Катя идёт.
examples.trans: Look, Katya is walking right this way.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ask for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Вон рядом стоит высокий Лёва, попроси его.
examples.trans: Tall Lyova is standing right there, ask him.

examples.text: Друзья, можно попросить минуту вашего внимания?
examples.trans: Friends, may I ask for a minute of your attention?

examples.text: Я прошу прощения.
examples.trans: I apologise.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'love', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.text: Прошу любить и уважать — Виктория Сергеевна!
examples.trans: Please welcome and respect—Viktoriya Sergeyevna!

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город.
examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Ты любишь жвачку?
examples.trans: Do you like gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'важать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'respect'.

examples.text: Прошу любить и уважать — Виктория Сергеевна!
examples.trans: Please welcome and respect—Viktoriya Sergeyevna!

examples.text: Уважайте суд!
examples.trans: Respect the court!

examples.text: Я тебя уважаю.
examples.trans: I respect you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, я новый директор ресторана «Клод Моне».
examples.trans: Hello, I am the new director of the Claude Monet restaurant.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, Аркадий Борисович!
examples.trans: Hello, Arkady Borisovich!

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Как дела?
examples.trans: Hello! How are you?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: Да мы сегодня не особо спешим.
examples.trans: We are not in much of a hurry today.

examples.text: В зале сегодня очень много заказов.
examples.trans: There are very many orders in the dining room today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе понравится моё новое предложение о покупке.
examples.trans: You will like my new purchase offer.

examples.text: Стой спокойно и красиво улыбайся.
examples.trans: Stand calmly and smile nicely.

examples.text: Давай беги отсюда, пока шеф не увидел.
examples.trans: Come on, run from here before Chef sees.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Ну, я просто так подумала.
examples.trans: Well, I just thought so.

examples.text: Лёва, ты ещё хорошо подумай.
examples.trans: Lyova, think about it some more.

examples.text: Не подумайте, что мы на электричестве экономим.
examples.trans: Do not think that we are skimping on electricity.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'являться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to appear'.

examples.text: Нам не надо появляться на работе вместе.
examples.trans: We do not need to appear at work together.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и появляться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to appear on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: Они совсем экономят на нашей культуре.
examples.trans: They are completely skimping on our culture.

examples.text: А что, она тебе совсем не нравится?
examples.trans: What, do you not like her at all?

examples.text: Мне новые отношения сейчас совсем не нужны.
examples.trans: I do not need a new relationship at all right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'стоятельство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'circumstances' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пока мы думаем, появляются совсем новые обстоятельства.
examples.trans: While we are thinking, completely new circumstances appear.

examples.text: Открылись новые обстоятельства по другому делу.
examples.trans: New circumstances have come to light in another case.

examples.text: Суд учёл новые обстоятельства дела.
examples.trans: The court considered the new circumstances of the case.
